case.title: Host/port split for a bound address

provenance.provenance_notes: Reconstructed from a real Flask bug fix: SERVER_NAME/host handling broke on IPv6 literal addresses like '[::1]:5000' because a naive str.partition(':') splits on the first colon, which also occurs inside the address itself. No Flask source or test text is reproduced -- function name, file path, and surrounding code are invented. The diff below is the reverse of the historical fix: it removes the bracket-aware branch to reintroduce the original defect mechanism.

diff: -        port = rest[1:] if rest.startswith(":") else None
return host, (port if sep else None)

ground_truth.explanation: Removing the bracket-aware branch makes every address parsed with a naive partition on the first colon. An IPv6 literal like '[::1]:5000' contains colons inside the address itself, so the naive split returns host='[' and a garbled port/host remainder instead of host='::1', port='5000' -- breaking any caller that binds, displays, or routes by host for IPv6 listeners.
